doc.title: Dick Griffin interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 12, 2024

title: Career highs: Abdullah Ibrahim, Marvin Gaye, Sun Ra and others
summary: Asked for a pinnacle, Griffin names five years with Abdullah Ibrahim, Marvin Gaye as best leader, friend Freddy Waite, Sun Ra, Kirk, Mingus, and Apollo house band work.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: This has been a most marvelous conversation. I want to wrap up with, this is sometimes a hard question. If you go to bed at night and you reflect on your career, is there a gig or a road trip or an association that comes to your mind as the pinnacle of what you’ve done?
Several, several, several in a sense.
I’ll give you several, that’s fine.

Okay. Well my stint with Abdullah Ibrahim, I played with him five years, enjoyed his music, learned a lot from him. That was the longest stint I’ve ever been with any particular band or situation. Then the best band leader that I work with and I always say stands out in my mind, Marvin Gaye, because of what he did after the gig. He would come down after all of the accolades and women being you know flirtatious and throwing their underwear on the bandstand. He would come down every night, look me in my eyes, shake my hand and say, “Man I really thank you for performing with me.” And my dear © Fillius Jazz Archive -21-

friend, like what we consider myself as a brother — because I never had a brother — Freddy Waite, we were in the first grade together and throughout college and everything it was a very strong influence. He was responsible for me getting in the band and doing a lot of things. But Marvin and I we used to talk about Freddy, how Freddy helped him play, you know taught him drums. Because Marvin could play the piano, he’d play the drums, he’d play several other instruments. So that one of the highlights of my life. Sun Ra was a highlight. As a teacher, performer Rahsaan Roland Kirk I liked. And Charles Mingus, my influence that I had for playing in his band. And believe it or not James Brown, some of those people that I played with at the Apollo Theater, ‘cause I played the house band at the Apollo Theater. Dionne Warwick, James Brown, Marvin Gaye. I actually played with Michael Jackson and Janet Jackson. I played with the Jacksons for a week at Radio City Hall so I got a chance to perform on the bandstand with those people, Michael Jackson and Janet Jackson.
